title: AMD-Backed MangoBoost Takes Aim at Nvidia's Inference Market with 'AI Factory'
source_used: BigGo Finance (full text from the main session's fulltext copy); no original outlet is named, and the page says it was compiled from the company's roadmap
key_facts: MangoBoost, a South Korean AI-infrastructure startup founded in 2022 by Seoul National University researchers and partnered with AMD, is building its own data centre in Seoul's Gangnam district and has launched 'Mango Inference'.
Mango Inference is a serverless inference service: companies run AI models through a single API key without building their own GPU infrastructure.

The first facility is a 1 MW 'AI factory' near Dosan Park; partial services have started, full construction is due by the first quarter of next year, with 5 MW planned within next year and 500 MW then gigawatt-class capacity in the US, Japan and Southeast Asia as long-term goals.

CTO Kwon Dong-up says software tuning of AMD Instinct GPUs gives performance comparable to or exceeding Nvidia's latest models and that the service is priced at least 20% below major rivals; CEO Kim Jang-woo says AMD has promised priority memory supply.

BigGo says MangoBoost made the first partner submission using multi-node AMD Instinct GPUs in the MLPerf Inference 5.0 benchmark and showed multi-region inference across South Korea and the US in InferenceX 6.0.
Kim says over 10 billion won (about $7.5 million) of revenue this year is attainable, and the company aims at trillions of won in revenue, with results from next year.
BigGo cites OpenRouter research: weekly token use reached 126 trillion in September, 250 times the January 2025 average, as AI agents use up to 1,000 times more tokens than a single chat.
quote_evidence: Our goal is to become a global company generating trillions of won in revenue.
We have priced our service at least 20% lower than major high-performance inference service providers.
MangoBoost achieves performance comparable to or exceeding Nvidia's latest models through software optimization alone.
why_it_matters_hint: A small startup is trying to sell cheaper AI-model hosting on AMD chips to challenge Nvidia, but the performance and price claims are the company's own.
event_date: 12 Oct 2026 (BigGo publication 06:55 UTC); the launch date is not stated
notes: BigGo's page is credited to its editorial team and says it was compiled from the company's expansion roadmap; most facts are company executives' statements, none checked independently. The quote_evidence lines are statements by the CEO and CTO as quoted by BigGo. 'Inference' means running a trained AI model to answer requests.
